correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts all possible numbers of original vertices in a minimal fort, including n=3. Each cut subdivision is forced, and the candidate cycles, original vertex set and star-cuts are individually proved minimal. Fort-hitting iff zero forcing follows by the first-force and terminal-white-fort arguments; therefore initial blue sets correspond exactly to nonempty original selections and coforest subdivision selections, with one excluded centered-star pair per original singleton. Labeled forest EGF and Cayley give every coefficient and optimal count. Direct brute-force checks of all forts and all forcing sets for n=3,4,5 and independent Prufer tree checks through n=7 completed VERIFY_OK. Infinite assertion rests on this exhaustive symbolic case proof, not the finite tests.

value.rationale: Minimal-fort hypergraphs and full zero forcing polynomials are natural studied objects. The prior known scalar optimum is strictly weaker than an explicit description of all obstructions and all forcing seed sizes. This theorem resolves all cardinality coefficients for an infinite two-layer incidence-graph family and provides a transparent Cayley spanning-tree classification and count of every minimum seed. This is a structural enumeration with motivated applications to graph monitoring, not a numerical restatement of the earlier scalar.
